chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Covering for brother Boston who cannot read music
summary: Smith hired his piano-playing brother Boston and covered for him and his bassist brother because neither read music.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Apart from the Ray Charles group, with the little groups that you had at this time, you were mainly using your brother Boston(?) on piano, weren't you?
Yeah.
Why was that?
Well, trying to help my people, you know. Blood's thicker than water, and he wanted to play, so I tried to help him. He'd stay with me long as I didn't stay away from town too long.
Did you help him with music at all? Did you sort of teach him at all?
I tried to teach him. He wouldn't stand no teaching.
Why is that?

Well, he just... In a way, he was just stupid. Tell the truth by now. He played with me up here in that big club, five years up there, and playing piano in that big band, and that woman didn't know that he couldn't read no music -- and he can't read none today. He didn't want to and don't want to!
Buster Smith - 191
Neither one of them.
Why do you think he doesn't?
Well, I think because I'm the leader and they could get by. I'll hold up for them. I cover up.
So you think it's laziness.

No, he wasn't lazy. He just didn't want to go to that trouble of trying to... In other words, it looked too much like right(?)/write(?). Tell the truth, it just looked too much... Because by me being the leader, he could get by, and I'd cover for him -- I covered and covered for both of them, many-many-many days and many years.
For both of them.
Yeah.
You're talking about your bass-playing brother as well.

Yeah. Bass player, too. Yeah, him too. He was with us when we were with Al Hibbler, and they throw out all that music at him, and they found out he couldn't read. So I told them, 'Well, I'll take care of him. I'll take him to the hotel and teach him, show him. Just follow me.'

Let me make this suggestion. Do you think that if you hadn't carried them, if you'd said, 'Look, I'd like to have you in my band, but you have to be able to make it, and I'll have to let you go until you get straight with the reading' and that sort of thing... Do you think that that, in the end, would have helped
Buster Smith - 192
them more, that they would have gone away and learned to read music?
Yeah, they would have.
Do you think you should have done that, then?

Yeah, I should have done that. Yeah, I should have. But we did this for pleasure. In other words, business is business and friendship's another. Yeah, that's what I'm saying. But I was trying to help them. Trying to help them.
